title: model-owned-projection-pipeline
universal_lens: A model-owned projection pipeline enforces architectural separation of concerns: model owns projections, sources own observations, contest engine owns constraints, evidence layer owns explanations, and registry owns promotion. This ensures that projections remain calibrated, versioned, and traceable.
gsi_mapping: GSI employs Bayesian inference to calibrate player and team distributions using historical labels and feature snapshots. Conformal prediction wraps outputs with uncertainty bounds, enabling risk-aware decision-making under epistemic constraints. GSI Mapping: Rooted in model-owned-projection-pipeline (45fe1473fd4bd2b7), this derivation preserves strict unit consistency, explicit validity boundaries, zero-leakage temporal separation, and bounded structural integration across GSI calibration heads, spectral orthogonalization clusters, and GSE Stage-2 situational reasoning families without fabricating parameters.
gse_mapping: GSE applies situational reasoning to transition between states defined by canonical entities, role availability, and feature materializations. State transitions are governed by deterministic logic layers that enforce consistency across time-varying inputs and constraints.

reasoning_traces.think:
The model-owned projection pipeline establishes a layered architecture where each component maintains distinct responsibilities. The decision spine resolves entities and temporal relationships, ensuring semantic clarity. The immutable ledger guarantees data integrity and traceability. Point-in-time feature materialization aligns inputs with model expectations. Role and availability models inject dynamic context into projections. These primitives form a coherent system where model ownership is preserved through all stages, preventing contamination from external heuristics or narratives. Failure modes arise when data integrity is compromised or when temporal alignment breaks down. Dualities emerge in how observations map to features and how role states influence outcome distributions. The pipeline supports retroactive evaluation and continuous learning via feedback loops.
